b1-15-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Film or Novel?
b1-15-01.scenario: You are Meg. It is Saturday evening in Budapest and you and Carlos are choosing what to do. He asks whether you would rather watch a film or read a novel.
b1-15-01.prompt: Tell Carlos which you prefer and give a reason.
cues: Say which you prefer, films or novels
Give a reason for your choice
b1-15-01.target: Prefiero las novelas porque puedo imaginar mejor a los personajes.
b1-15-01.english: I prefer novels because I can imagine the characters better.
b1-15-01.canDo: I can express preferences about films, books and music.

b1-15-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What Did You Think?
b1-15-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg saw a film in Budapest on Friday evening. Meg asks what you thought of it.
b1-15-02.prompt: Tell Meg what you think of the plot and the characters.
cues: Give your view of the plot
Give your view of the characters
b1-15-02.target: El argumento resulta convincente y los personajes están bien desarrollados.
b1-15-02.english: The plot is convincing and the characters are well developed.
b1-15-02.canDo: I can evaluate cultural works using specific criteria.

b1-15-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Film to Watch
b1-15-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos is looking for something to watch this weekend in Budapest. You saw a film last week and loved it.
b1-15-03.prompt: Recommend the film to Carlos and say why.
cues: Recommend that he watches the film
Give a reason about the plot
b1-15-03.target: Te recomiendo que veas esta película porque el argumento resulta convincente.
b1-15-03.english: I recommend that you watch this film because the plot is convincing.
b1-15-03.canDo: I can recommend cultural works to another person.

b1-15-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Film and Novel
b1-15-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg is reading a novel that was made into a film, and she asks how the two compare.
b1-15-04.prompt: Compare the film with the novel for Meg.
cues: Add a fact about the novel
b1-15-04.target: La película es más breve que la novela, que tiene un protagonista muy interesante.
b1-15-04.english: The film is shorter than the novel, which has a very interesting protagonist.
b1-15-04.canDo: I can compare films, books and other works.

b1-15-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Night at the Theatre
b1-15-05.scenario: You are Meg. You have just read a short story about a night at the theatre and you tell Carlos what the narrator thinks of the actor and the actress.
b1-15-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the narrator thinks of the actor and of the actress.
cues: Say what the narrator thinks of the actor
Say why the narrator loves the actress
b1-15-05.target: Piensa que el actor es bueno, pero le encanta la actriz porque tiene una voz muy buena.
b1-15-05.english: The narrator thinks the actor is good, but loves the actress because she has a very good voice.
b1-15-05.canDo: I can write a connected cultural review.

b1-15-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Should I Read It?
b1-15-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you about a novel you have just read in Budapest and whether she should read it too.
b1-15-consolidation.prompt: Give Meg your evaluation and a recommendation.
cues: Say what you think of the novel
b1-15-consolidation.target: Me parece una novela original y te recomiendo que la leas.
b1-15-consolidation.english: The novel seems original to me and I recommend that you read it.
b1-15-consolidation.canDo: I can consolidate culture and entertainment vocabulary.
